challenges.title: Burp Suite-CTF
challenges.tagline: Act as an external red teamer investigating the fintech company MegaCorp. Every flag needs Burp Suite Community Edition and nothing else.
description: A whistleblower has hidden flags across MegaCorp's infrastructure and you have been hired to recover them. The one rule: if a flag can be reached without touching a specific Burp Community feature, the challenge has failed its purpose.

The CTF is split into six self-contained missions of roughly three to five hours each, because Burp Community cannot save projects. Every mission's flags are locked in as you go, so a crash only costs the mission you were in.
learn: Proxy: interception, history filters, match and replace, WebSockets
Repeater and Inspector: chaining requests, race conditions, request smuggling
Intruder: throttle-aware attacks with small, smart wordlists
Sequencer, Decoder and Comparer: session analysis and multi-layer decoding
requirements: Burp Suite Community Edition (pre-installed on Kali Linux)
Docker with Compose v2.17 or newer
Roughly 4 GB of free RAM and a few GB of disk for lab images
Firefox, Chrome, Edge or Brave for the launcher extension

intro: You are Nils Berg, an external penetration tester hired by a whistleblower inside MegaCorp - a mid-sized fintech under investigation for fraud. The whistleblower has deliberately exposed fragments of evidence across nine services on the company's external perimeter. Each fragment is a flag, formatted FLAG{...}.

Your job is to prove the breach is possible. The catch: MegaCorp's infrastructure is deliberately fussy. Nothing works out of the box. Before you find a single flag, you must configure your tool - Burp Suite Community Edition - against nine different quirks of their setup.
setup: Open Burp Suite Community Edition. In Kali Linux, it's pre-installed. On other systems, download it from portswigger.net/burp/communitydownload.

Set up Burp's CA certificate in your browser: with Burp running, visit http://burp/cert, download cacert.der, and import it into Firefox under Settings, Privacy & Security, Certificates, View Certificates, Authorities, Import. Tick 'Trust this CA to identify websites.'

Configure Firefox to route traffic through Burp: Settings, General, Network Settings, Manual proxy. HTTP Proxy and SSL Proxy both = 127.0.0.1, port 8080 (Burp's default). Tick 'Also use this proxy for HTTPS.'
In Burp, make sure Proxy, Intercept is set to 'Intercept is off' so traffic flows by default. You will turn it on when you need to pause and modify requests.
Start the lab. The button below will launch it and give you the entry point URL. From there, your browser is your main tool - but Burp is doing the work.

hints.text: Flag 1 is not visible in the page content. Where does Burp keep the requests it has seen? Try the Proxy, HTTP history tab.
Flag 2 lives on a port your proxy is not listening on. Burp can listen on more than one port at once - check Proxy settings, Proxy listeners.
Flag 3 needs a client certificate. The mission bundle ships one in the certs/ folder. In Burp, it goes under Proxy settings, TLS, Client TLS certificates.

labs.title: Mission 1: Setup & Recon
labs.summary: Configure Burp against MegaCorp's fussy environments: CA certificates, listeners, client certs, SOCKS upstream, NTLM, HTTP/2.

objectives.title: The HTTPS Portal
objectives.task: A MegaCorp portal at portal.megacorp.local hides something in its response headers. You will only see it if your tool is intercepting TLS traffic.

objectives.title: The Second Listener
objectives.task: One of MegaCorp's services is on a port your proxy is not listening on. Find it, and adjust your proxy.

objectives.title: The Client Certificate Gate
objectives.task: A legacy host refuses to speak to you unless you present a specific client certificate. The certificate you need is bundled with the mission.

objectives.title: The Hidden Internal Host
objectives.task: A service on MegaCorp's internal network is unreachable directly. There is a way through - but not a direct one.

objectives.title: The NTLM Wall
objectives.task: An intranet service rejects anonymous requests. It demands NTLM authentication. Your tool can carry it.

objectives.title: The Modern-Only Endpoint
objectives.task: A service responds only over HTTP/2. Over HTTP/1.1, it politely declines. Your tool can be told which protocol to use.

objectives.title: The Ghost Hostname
objectives.task: One hostname has no DNS record. Your browser cannot resolve it. But your tool can be told where to look.

objectives.title: The Hidden JSON Route
objectives.task: An API endpoint isn't linked from any page. It only surfaces when you filter your site map by content type.

objectives.title: The Broken Certificate
objectives.task: A MegaCorp service presents an expired certificate. When the handshake fails, your tool logs why. Read the log carefully.

labs.title: Mission 2: Interception & History
labs.summary: Manipulate live traffic and dig through proxy history: role tampering, WebSockets, match and replace rules.

labs.title: Mission 3: Repeater & Inspector
labs.summary: Surgical exploitation of the API and payment services: chained calls, race conditions, request smuggling.

labs.title: Mission 4: Intruder Mastery
labs.summary: Brute-force work sized for Community's throttled Intruder: PINs, pitchfork attacks, token chains.

labs.title: Mission 5: Sequencer, Decoder, Comparer & Sessions
labs.summary: Cryptographic and session-layer analysis of MegaCorp's token handling, macros and cookie jar.

labs.title: Mission 6: Client-Side, Extensions & Finale
labs.summary: DOM XSS, clickjacking, Logger-only flags, JWT forging, then decrypt the CEO's secret.
